PORTFOLIO PROJECT · PROTOTYPE IN PROGRESS

A little more room
to be human.

Building a portfolio you can ride through—without making anyone work to read it.

ProjectThis portfolioFocusExploration & clarityStagePlayable study
The intentThe decisionsWhat comes next

THE INTENT

Personality shouldn’t cost clarity.

I’m a UX designer who enjoys meeting people, singing, and photographing clouds. A conventional portfolio can show my work clearly. The playful mode gives those interests a place to live.

Early world concepts tried to fit too much into one view. The correction was spatial: spread destinations out, follow the rider, and let each place arrive when it matters.

This portfolio is a working design study. The five project readers use original project documents, with evidence and limitations shown together.

AT THE WORKBENCH

Choose a layer. See the decision.

A route with something around the bend.

The first circular track felt repetitive. A winding circuit now alternates long sweeps, tighter bends and two bridge crossings. Short pull-offs lead to five personal stops.

Trade-off: a longer route asks for more time. The map can take you to a stop, or open its story immediately.

THE DECISIONS

Small choices. A calmer ride.

01 Discover one place at a time

The camera follows a visible rider at a stable angle. Open ground separates the arrival, project stop and bridge. The full route is never forced into the default gameplay view.

Trade-off: more distance between stops. Click-to-ride and direct reading keep that distance optional.

02 A bicycle with forgiving controls

Pedaling and coasting bring a human pace to the world. The bicycle balances automatically, turns even at low speed, and brakes on Space. No cycling skill or racing objective is required.

Trade-off: gentler handling is less realistic. Approaching a case study comfortably matters more than simulating a race.

03 Stop the world. Let the story speak.

Case studies open as selectable, scrollable HTML. Riding pauses, held keys clear, and closing the story returns to the same place. Keyboard focus stays inside the reader until it closes.

Trade-off: the reader covers most of the scene. That separation protects reading from competing motion.

04 An exit you never need to hunt for

The Portfolio / Play switch stays in a consistent screen position while riding and remains available inside each reader. Press P while riding for a direct return to the portfolio. Switching modes keeps your place in the world. Normal mode uses the same project stories, with category filters and a direct route into the work.

The world has local signs and contextual actions. It doesn’t repeat a conventional website menu over the scene.

THE NEXT TEST

Feel it before filling it.

Five personal places now connect reading and exploration. Direction boards guide the route, while Mochiy Pop P One headings and DM Sans text keep the experience consistent.

  • Observe where first-time visitors hesitate.
  • Tune camera distance, stopping and signs from actual use.
  • Add original cloud photographs and vocal recordings.
  • Check whether each stop feels personal without distracting from the work.

No participant-study results or business outcomes are claimed for this portfolio.
